subject.title: feat: heading-aware chunking + entity extraction for memory search

question: Should OpenClaw implement heading-aware chunking now as a narrow memory-core change, and if so should it be default behavior or an explicit strategy option?
rationale: The source path is clear, but changing chunk boundaries affects existing indexes and retrieval behavior; adding a config strategy also conflicts with the repo’s high bar for new config surface.

options.title: Approve narrow default
options.body: Implement heading-aware markdown boundaries as the default chunking behavior for structured memory files, with no-heading behavior preserved and index metadata forcing reindex.

options.title: Require explicit strategy
options.body: Add a documented chunking strategy option and reindex metadata, accepting the extra config surface to avoid changing existing heading-heavy workspaces by default.

options.title: Defer to Memory MVP
options.body: Keep this issue parked under the broader memory ingestion/entity direction and avoid a standalone chunker change until that design is settled.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow default
recommendation.body: Implement heading-aware markdown boundaries as the default chunking behavior for structured memory files, with no-heading behavior preserved and index metadata forcing reindex.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent memory-core refactor history makes this the closest routing candidate for deciding the current memory-core boundary.
